question_text: There are three branches of government. Why?
lead_in: You only need to give one reason:

official_answers.text: So one part does not become too powerful

why_it_matters.text: Splitting power into three branches means no one branch can grab too much. Each can check the others — the president can veto laws, the courts can strike them down, Congress can override the president. That tug-of-war was designed on purpose. Slow and messy, but it prevents tyranny.

fun_fact.text: James Madison explained why we need three separate branches in one perfect line in Federalist Paper No. 51 (1788): 'If men were angels, no government would be necessary.' His point: people aren't perfect, so power needs to check power. Split government in three, and no single piece can get too strong.
